summary: A note from Alex McKenzie at BBN with network traffic statistics for July 1972. BBN had given ARPA a monthly summary of host packets output and, after requests, agreed to publish them as RFCs. The figures are monthly totals or overall averages. It was replaced by RFC 391.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 378 publishes BBN's packet-output statistics for ARPANET hosts in July 1972. The tables separate inter-node packets from intra-node packets and report totals or overall averages.

subtitle: BBN's monthly summary of ARPANET host packet output for July 1972.

tldr.problem: ARPA and network sites requested access to the monthly host packet-output statistics that BBN had been supplying to ARPA.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC publishes July 1972 packet-output totals and averages by host, separating inter-node and intra-node packets.
tldr.outcome: RFC 378 is a traffic-statistics report and was obsoleted by RFC 391.

today: RFC 378 is a July 1972 ARPANET traffic report and was obsoleted by RFC 391.

sections.title: Purpose and Limits of the Statistics
sections.content:
BBN had supplied ARPA with a monthly summary of host packets output for several months. After questions from sites, ARPA agreed to publish the statistics in RFC form. RFC 378 contains the figures for July 1972.

The RFC warns that numbers are monthly totals or overall averages based on 24 hours per day and 7 days per week. They are not useful for determining peak traffic conditions. The table notes missing data for 17 days.
sections.plainLanguage: The report shows monthly traffic counts, not busy-hour peaks. It also notes that data was missing for 17 days.

sections.title: Host Packet Output
sections.content:
For each listed host, the table reports inter-node packets, intra-node packets, and a total. Some rows also include average daily internode packets and the number of days represented.

The summary gives 15,056,880 inter-node packets and 13,825,310 intra-node packets. The report also gives daily averages of 501,896 inter-node and 460,844 intra-node packets, and an average of 1.09 packets per inter-node message.
sections.plainLanguage: The table separates packets sent between hosts from packets counted within a host. The summary also reports daily averages and an average packet count per inter-node message.

sections.title: Status of the Report
sections.content:
RFC 378 is a statistical snapshot for July 1972. It presents measured totals and averages; it does not define a protocol or explain peak network load.

The unit metadata records RFC 391 as the later RFC that obsoleted this report.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC records a month's packet statistics. A later traffic report replaced it.
